```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

A 5 cm mosaic of 300 ha weighs several GB: one date is slow to display, a whole series cannot be stacked.
`aggregate_mosaics()` makes, for each mosaic, a version at 0.5 m (or any other resolution) with the bands R, G, B
and, if asked, RGB spectral indices, all on the same grid.

```{r}
library(canobsR)
aggregate_mosaics("D:/bouamir/3_aligned", "D:/bouamir/4_mosaics_50cm",
                  indices = c("GCC", "RCC", "BCC", "GLI", "VARI", "NDYI"))
```

```
10 mosaics -> D:/bouamir/4_mosaics_50cm: 0.5 m, bands R, G, B, GCC, RCC, BCC, GLI, VARI, NDYI; common grid 1850 x 1720 m
[1/10] 20220427_50cm.tif: 287.4 ha, 212 s; remaining about 32 min
...
```

## What is in the files

* `out_dir/<mosaic name>_50cm.tif` (`_1m` at 1 m, ...): float32, one band per variable, **named** (`R`, `G`, `B`,
  then the indices in the order asked).
* Each value is the **mean of the pixels of the mosaic in the cell**. The indices are computed on each pixel (5 cm),
  then averaged: the mean of the index, not the index of the mean colour (they differ where the cell mixes crowns,
  gaps and shadows).
* **One grid for all the dates**, aligned on multiples of the resolution and covering all the mosaics: the dates
  overlay exactly, and the whole series can be stacked:

```{r}
f <- list.files("D:/bouamir/4_mosaics_50cm", pattern = "_50cm\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE)
s <- terra::rast(f)                               # all dates, all bands
gcc <- s[names(s) == "GCC"]                       # one layer per date
names(gcc) <- substr(basename(f), 1, 8)
```

* The background of the mosaics (white, or black, in the 3 bands) is no data; a cell is no data (NaN) when less
  than half of it is covered by the mosaic (`min_coverage`).
* Run it again after new dates: the mosaics already done are skipped (`overwrite = TRUE` makes them again).
  New dates that extend the site enlarge the common grid: the alignment of the cells is the same, but the files of
  the earlier dates then have a smaller extent (`terra::extend()` before stacking, or `overwrite = TRUE`).

## The indices

```{r}
rgb_indices()
```

| Name | Formula | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| GCC, RCC, BCC | G, R, B / (R + G + B) (chromatic coordinates) | Richardson et al. 2007 |
| ExG | 2g - r - b | Woebbecke et al. 1995 |
| ExR | 1.4r - g | Meyer et al. 1998 |
| ExGR | ExG - ExR | Meyer & Neto 2008 |
| GLI | (2G - R - B) / (2G + R + B) | Louhaichi et al. 2001 |
| VARI | (G - R) / (G + R - B), bounded to [-1, 1] | Gitelson et al. 2002 |
| NGRDI | (G - R) / (G + R) | Tucker 1979 |
| NDYI | (G - B) / (G + B) | Sulik & Long 2016 |
| MGRVI | (G² - R²) / (G² + R²) | Bendig et al. 2015 |
| RGBVI | (G² - R B) / (G² + R B) | Bendig et al. 2015 |
| TGI | G - 0.39 R - 0.61 B | Hunt et al. 2013 |
| CIVE | 0.441 R - 0.811 G + 0.385 B + 18.787 | Kataoka et al. 2003 |
| VEG | G / (R^0.667 B^0.333) | Hague et al. 2006 |
| BI | sqrt((R² + G² + B²) / 3) (brightness) | |
| SAT | (max - min) / max of R, G, B (saturation) | |

R, G, B are the digital numbers (0-255) of the mosaic; r, g, b the chromatic coordinates. `indices = "all"` adds
all of them. Pixels where an index is undefined (division by zero) are left out of the mean of that index only.

The colour calibration made by `generate_mosaics()` (white balance per image, vignetting) makes the indices of the
dates of a chunk comparable; between chunks, the colours can still differ slightly (light, season): indices that
are ratios (GCC, NDYI, ...) are the least sensitive to it.
